candidates.name: eurostat (rOpenGov)
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (and Python sibling 'eurostat' bindings exist too) that pulls any Eurostat table via API/bulk download, including avia_paoc (air passenger transport by type of schedule/coverage/country) and avia_paocc (bilateral country pairs). avia_paoc alone covers 1993 through Q2 2026 (per live query), ~2.6M cell values across EU/EEA + UK/CH reporting countries, quarterly and annual granularity by country and some airport groupings; avia_paocc ~11.6M values for bilateral passenger flows. search_eurostat()/get_eurostat() functions handle discovery and download; data updates continuously as Eurostat republishes.
candidates.why_useful: Gives a maintained, one-command route to official EU-wide air passenger transport statistics (a leading indicator of European travel demand / cross-border trip volume) at quarterly granularity back to 1993 - directly usable as a European travel-volume regressor for ABNB's EMEA nights, addressing the travel_volume_transport gap with a much longer, cleaner history than any single-airport scraper.
candidates.time_coverage: 1993-2026 (quarterly, with normal Eurostat 1-2 quarter reporting lag)
candidates.geography: EU27 + EEA + UK/Switzerland, country-level (some sub-national/airport breakdowns exist in the underlying avia_ dataset family)
candidates.size_hint: avia_paoc ~2.6M values, avia_paocc ~11.6M values (full table incl. all countries/years)
candidates.last_activity: actively maintained rOpenGov package, data refreshes live from Eurostat

candidates.name: daio (EUROCONTROL PRU)
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed CSV and Parquet files (daio_2019.csv ... daio_2026.csv, plus .parquet equivalents) of DAILY flight counts by EUROCONTROL Member State: departures, arrivals, internal, overflight, circular flights, and combined DAIO/dep+arr totals, by UTC date and country name, 2019 through 2026 (present-day, via update_data.sh automation).
candidates.why_useful: A daily, country-level European flight-volume series is a real-time-ish proxy for cross-border air travel activity feeding short-haul European trip demand (nights bookings in EU markets); daily granularity through the current year is unusually fresh for a committed GitHub dataset and could nowcast intra-quarter European travel momentum ahead of Eurostat's lagged passenger releases.
candidates.geography: EUROCONTROL Member States (all of Europe incl. UK, Turkey, etc.), country-level (not airport-level)
candidates.size_hint: 8 annual CSV/Parquet file pairs, daily rows x ~40 countries x ~7 flight-count columns
candidates.license: Not confirmed (EUROCONTROL PRU open-data project; check repo LICENSE before use)
candidates.last_activity: actively updated via automated script (data through 2026 present)

candidates.name: OPDI (Open Performance Data Initiative)
candidates.what_it_holds: Pip-installable Python ETL pipeline that processes raw ADS-B state-vector data from OpenSky Network's S3 store into enriched flight-trajectory tables (flight IDs, departure/arrival aerodromes ADEP/ADES, flight phases, FL crossings, airport events) for ~1,036 European aerodromes (lon -31..46, lat 33..79).
candidates.why_useful: Could be used to derive flight-count-by-airport time series as an alternate traffic proxy, but requires running the pipeline against OpenSky's raw archive (heavy compute, no committed output dataset) - a method, not a ready dataset; lower immediate usefulness than daio or eurostat.
candidates.time_coverage: Depends on OpenSky Network archive availability (generally 2019-present for ADS-B coverage)
candidates.geography: Europe + North Africa/Middle East extension noted as incomplete

candidates.name: pruatlas
candidates.what_it_holds: R package bundling GIS objects (not CSV): EUROCONTROL FIRs (Flight Information Regions) from Network Manager, ANSPs from the ACE Benchmarking Report, and world country boundaries, based on a single AIRAC cycle from late 2015 (AIRAC 1512).
candidates.why_useful: Pure airspace geography/mapping utility, no passenger or traffic volume figures; only useful as a plotting aid if building airspace maps, not a KPI input.

candidates.name: airport-dashboard (EUROCONTROL PRU)
candidates.what_it_holds: Interactive dashboard source (framework, not verified in depth) for airport performance metrics across the PRU network; likely pulls from PRU's own data services rather than shipping a standalone dataset file.
candidates.why_useful: Points to where EUROCONTROL PRU publishes airport performance/traffic metrics; worth a deeper look (not verified beyond org listing) as a possible source of committed data files or an API client for punctuality/traffic KPIs by airport.
candidates.geography: European airports in the PRU network
candidates.last_activity: listed among 79 active EUROCONTROL PRU org repos

candidates.name: Heathrow-noise (BBC Data Unit)
candidates.what_it_holds: BBC Data Unit journalism repo scraping Heathrow's public noise-complaint portal, logging aircraft landing/noise complaint events roughly every five minutes; a byproduct data trail of landing frequency rather than an official passenger count.
candidates.why_useful: Landing-frequency-as-noise-complaint-count could be a rough proxy for Heathrow flight cadence, but it's noise-complaint volume (confounded by public complaint behavior, not raw traffic) and a one-off journalism scrape, not an ongoing dataset - marginal use only if nothing else is available for high-frequency Heathrow activity.
candidates.last_activity: unspecified, appears to be a completed one-off data-journalism project

candidates.name: lhrnet
candidates.what_it_holds: Neural-network project predicting Heathrow runway direction/usage from OpenSky-derived flight data; a modeling exercise built on live OpenSky pulls, no committed historical passenger or flight-count dataset of its own.
candidates.why_useful: Not a data source per se; runway-usage prediction is orthogonal to passenger volume. Low relevance beyond illustrating another OpenSky-based Heathrow project.
candidates.time_coverage: unspecified (live OpenSky data at time of project)
